newsitem.title: CHINA: China auctions gold tickets for Beijing-HK train.
newsitem.headline: China auctions gold tickets for Beijing-HK train.

text.p: China auctioned eight sets of gold commemorative tickets on Saturday for the inaugural train journey from Beijing to Hong Kong, which reverts to Chinese rule on July 1.

Officials of the Pacific (International) Auction Co voiced delight with the success of the auction, which earned 403,600 yuan ($48,626). The auction house sold all eight sets, each comprising one gold and one silver ticket, before a crowded audience in Beijing.

The highest bid for a single set of the tickets to commemorate the inaugural train that sets off from Beijing on Sunday was 57,200 ($6,800), said Jee Tao, manager of the auction house project department. The lowest price was 33,000 yuan.
"These tickets have a great collectors' value," said one successful bidder, who declined to be identified.

Most buyers declined to say what they would do with their tickets, which are not valid. But one elderly couple, who paid the second highest price of 52,800 yuan for their set, said they would present the tickets to relatives in Hong Kong.
The first train from Hong Kong to the Chinese capital leaves on Monday, and the 30-hour ride promises airline style luxury, a far cry from China's crammed and sweaty domestic trains.
Hong Kong, a British colony of 156 years, reverts to China at midnight on June 30.
